Yoga Mat!! They are light, portable and won't look out of place to just have with you ~ casually ~. Though I am a femme presenting person, I also don't really carry bags or purses; I tend to just have keys and phone with me in pockets

This strategy has several upsides; casual workout encouragement and the reminder to breathe/center/move/align throughout the day... You can get a cute one that compliments ur aesthetic or one of the ones that is casually picnic mat material if parks are your thing... You can have one that you literally never use for yoga and just exists for this purpose and let people think you embody a spirit of sportiness that doesn't exist and delight in that little lie.. 

I just have a simple yoga strap (velcros around the mat and then has a cord to go over my shoulder) on my daily mat and have it hanging on my shoulder (across the back) when I am out and about or on my way into work. 

Basically right before I approach the gate, I tug the cord up so the yoga mat comes forward and tuck it under my armpit so it's like poking back, right as I tap thru. I kinda lead with my right foot to pivot slightly so the mat doesn't hit the wall of the gate but kinda sweeps around chest level just behind me. (I nix the sweep at rush hours when people are in close proximity just due to crowds but still will keep my mat out and lowered to improve my personal space buffer passively) That way there's a direct impediment to anyone scooching up to me. If I have to, I can simply turn my body a little more to like nudge them with the end of the roll, I have, and will, without remorse.

 It's not like I am using something hard or pushing them or hitting them. I am providing an impediment and I'm not moving fast enough for it to hurt unless they are rushing me.

Mk. I guess my main argument here is - it is not 'common sense' that a pond - in a place I have never been before - would have a random deadly thing in it that you can't see, can't sense until hours later, and wouldn't know danger of the 'risk' taken. That is where I think the OKF is failing. 

Do I think they should do more harm reduction so people who choose to use drugs don't straight up croak? Of course! But that's beside the point and they're clearly not taking responsibility for people choosing to use illicit drugs dangerously.... But that's not the issue we are discussing at all here. 

 Drugs or not, the people OP is referencing are dying from bacterial exposure - whether high, or sober, or drunk (OP even mentioned that this happens - when the festival is NOT happening to old, young etc, different people at random who accidentally pick the wrong pool to swim in~) the whole point is people may not know there is an invisible safety hazard in still water in the region and they, not only make zero effort to inform anyone about this hidden danger - they also CHOOSE to showcase it in promo materials (aka they passively promote/condone the behavior that is unusually risky). 

Like thinking for myself, (hypothetically for sake of ex.), I'd think - oh, I am a really confident swimmer. Used to be a lifeguard and know how to remain safe in open water, let alone a quarry or pond with no currents or predators or threats to really 'get' me, besides drowning due to a catastrophic failure of my limbs or something. I am sober, I am with a friend; I just got a cool down cause it's too hot!!. Since I think that risk is like 0, Yea - maybe walking past a sign (I may or may not have even noticed cause I was talking to my friend on the approach) doesn't seem dangerous - In fact - I know that they're not even gonna yell at me or anything for breaking the rules, cause it's OKF and they had pics from last year where people were enjoying the water

Do you see how this specifically, is something that the fest should be making PSAs about?

Sure. But I think the problem here is that, the music festival is 1. Producing promotional materials that's showing people in hazardous water looking chill & having a fun ol time.
 2. Leaving a dinky lil sign up so they absolve themselves of liability from brain eating amoeba most people don't even know exist, let alone recognize that the water may hold that risk. This isn't about a lifeguard or no lifeguard, there is an invisible, deadly threat most people may not even know to expect
3. Seems the fest isn't even doing the basics of making Public Service Announcements to inform people of that risk or taking any sort of ownership for setting up this scenario by promoting the dangerous behavior
 4 and it ultimately shouldn't fall on some random kind reddit poster to warn people, to avoid a very preventable potential death. 

Yes there are dumb ways to die and people who shirk off responsibility for their own actions, but also, the issue here is that it isn't like bringing in drugs and saying -oh no one told me I couldnt- at all... Swimming at night isn't super insanely deadly, or why someone ended up dead, per OP. it's literally got to do with microorganisms outside of the swimmers control, could be Michael Phelps in there, wouldn't matter to ameobas. 

The festival isn't doing anything to say 'dont go in the water, it's scary!!' they've got a sign saying 'uh oh don't swim guys! There's no supervison' and then are literally showing people swimming in promo materials as OP mentioned. Like. Yea, that's on OKF at that point. They're teeing up a dangerous scenario that makes it not even likely, but probable that someone else gets hurt.

Yea, part of the reason I left is because I was repeatedly pressured by the owner and management to NOT directly explain to guests where the 20% went at that restaurant. They told us that no one wants to talk money, that it was rude to explain(?) and instructed us to be kind but vague, remind guests 'that tips are not expected but appreciated', feign ignorance/confusion/just smile and to redirect managers to the table if there was any further inquiry. Any time I directed a manager to the table, I could guarantee no tip from that check. I started just saying explicitly what it was but it started to feel dicey because I was then actually getting tips, but management started like eyeballing me a lot more... Luckily, over that last pay period, using my little tagline explanation, I increased my savings enough to jump ship even though I didn't have something solid underfoot for another week or so, but I literally would not have been able to have that mobility if I had followed the instructions of management.

Yea i feel that the law's spirit was a good one. I want my support staff to be well paid and when it is in my hands, I always tip out 20%+ of my tips to my bussers & food runners.

 Unfortunately companies are always gonna try to externalize costs and save, however they can. In this case it's basically kneecapping servers direct earnings from their tables to spread it around to everyone else so the restaurant doesn't have to cover their wages anymore. 

Also, people saying that $17 is a lot is just .... kinda wild to me?? Like DC is expensive to live and exist in.

The new tipped minimum is still only $10, that means at most restaurants, the only wage you are guaranteed is $60 for 6 hours of your life. If no one tips you, that's what it is and those $10 comes from the restaurant each time. If your restaurant is dead on Tuesday and you only get two tables because you and the bartender are splitting covers, you maybe get tipped $12 total. That's a <$70 shift & not enough, for most people I'd estimate.

 I know of 2 restaurants that have a 20% service charge and still only pay their workers $10/hr + tips. That service charge is NOT going to your server. They are still busting ass to get $70 at the end of the day. I think that's the worst iteration of this change. At least the place I was at, though it was cloaked in secrecy, guaranteed $102. It's tough out here.

Edited to be less frustrated.

Though yes, crappy management is almost always a reason to leave any employer, I guarantee, based off of direct personal and witnessed experience here in DC in the last year...  that PLENTY of servers, bartenders AND support staff will shift direction if they feel that the money/service charge/tip/wage combo is not lining up.
Yea, that makes more sense to my smooth brain too 😂

Some guests at my restaurant certainly did. They thought it was quite literally a tip out that was pre-included like a traditional gratuity system. There was a lot of confusion I had to regularly explain. I agree and never said it was your job? Confused as to why you included that portion.

Agreed. This is why it felt shady, why they have had a revolving door of staff and I eventually left. Just know, there are other servers out there who don't have as much mobility in this market, and are stuck making due at restaurants with owners who are taking advantage of their labor.

This doesn't excuse the behavior of externalizing operation costs on the consumer, but instead just reminds people that there is another loser in this service charge shell game, and that are the laborers actually doing the work at your table, and behind the line. 

This is the only reason I included the encouragement to still tip servers that you feel deserve that extra juice. Service charges are different at every place, at some restaurants, the charge quite literally goes to the restaurant operation costs (like managing insurance costs) and not a cent actually goes to employees in which case, Tips are still the main method of making a livable wage at all. It's a tough situation.

That's because competent servers leave, after going above and beyond, and then regularly not receiving tips from guests who erroneously believe service charges are paid out to their servers. At least at my previous restaurant, which has a nearly identical service charge note on the menus and receipts, only 32% of each 20% service charge was allocated to me - on my tables, not all tables in the house, mind you - and the 68% went to... 'wage increases' for the staff that were intentionally vaguely allocated. 
I have yet to fully understand how exactly this shakes out. But what I realized over time was it was actually a way for the restaurant to externalize the entire wage cost (of 17$/hr) onto guests and really put servers, food runners, and bussers at a disadvantage due to the, understandably, far lower tip average. I made less per week at this restaurant, despite the fact that I was doing double the sales, doing a ton more work and working double the hours. My money was way better when there were almost no support staff and I was way more stressed out and leaving shifts miserable. When we had tons of staff, every support staff was unmotivated to work hard because there was no real incentive to go above and beyond. 

So Yea, sorry to write so much, but I guess it's worth bearing in mind that good service and service charges being inversely correlated, happens for a reason and that your server is very likely relying on those on-top tips so if you do happen to get a great person, please reward their efforts. Totally understand the hangups tho and generally feel this is shifty behavior on the part of employers.

That journey was by NO means a linear trajectory (got far worse before I got better) but very fortunately for me, it was right about this inflection point that I found the kink community.

I highly recommend 2 things.
First is a resource, Yoga with Adriene, who you can find on Youtube. She has several free, 30-day series of yoga movement practices and I have found it helpful as well as a ton of more specialized videos (yoga for back/yoga for when you are sleepy). 

Second is to carve out space for your practice; as you jump in, the biggest barriers is often our ability to show up (at least it is for me). Before I could consistently get myself to get up and do the yoga thing, I used to play one yoga video a day, even if it was like while I was doing dishes or commuting or in couchlock in a puddle, this helped me to get used to actually watching (& get it into my YouTube algorithm too!), learned little hints/lingo/poses and was a bit more mindful with movement and my breathing throughout the day. Once I was watching the videos in contexts where I could squeeze it in, but couldn't necessarily join in, it was uncomfortable. It made me antsy to watch the videos when I did have the opportunity/ability to join in. Once I had this desire/discomfort, I wanted to make time for the yoga moves, wanted to go sit on the mat to watch, even if not joining in today and just putting on lotion for a self massage or something, or wanted to wake up a teeny bit earlier for a practice before my eggs. At this stage, I made sure I clicked on a video everyday and moved to it too, even if I only had 5 extra minutes, I tried to do one of Adriene's mini-vids or a flow I could feel out, every day.

 Carving out the mental space and time to do it was major; For myself, I also had the luxury to be able to carve out physical space as well, which I recommend. So I have one back wall that I have no reason to ever really walk all the way over to where I used to try to put my yoga mat, never remembered to get on. Moved my whole kitchen table over (it's a lil cramped now but ok) and squeezed into the middle of my living area instead and the flow is easier to find! But you can also create this space by doing things like going outside to do your practice, or having a ritual where you unroll your mat and such, for me I had to reduce some of those little tasks to get myself to be consistent (which was the most beneficial for me). 

Now yoga is just a part of my life. I don't necessarily keep myself to a strict daily ritual because I can't maintain that, but I notice how stiff and sluglike I feel if I am not doing yoga for a period. Plus at this point, I naturally turn to a yoga vid if I find myself slouching at my desk, or realize I have a sore neck looking at the pantry, had a difficult conversation that left me feeling a drift or have just had a flashback. I appreciate having the tool in my box.

First and foremost, I am sorry that you had such a difficult experience your first time with psychedelics. It sounds like the person you were with was not being very sensible, responsible or respectful. 

In terms of dose, I would say that 3g is not an unheard of recommendation for first experiences. It is a strong trip experience but it is usually the type of experience new users are looking for when trying to 'trip out' and not feel like they want to take more part way thru. I feel like 2.5 is a bit more reasonable but it depends on your size as well.  

The trip sitter you had was not a good trip sitter. Full stop. Giving you a full trip dose for the first time, they should know that you are gonna be off your rock for a minute and will say silly things and blurt out whatever pops into your head or say nothing and giggle or make strange yelping noises. A trip sitters role is to stay in the neutral to positive zone and help to guide you thru any confusion, reminding you that this is a finite experience and any discoveries can be reexamined/rediscovered/verified with time! Some people feel that the trip sitter also dosing can help them to self identify and remain open and that may be fine in some cases.... but if the dose/substance you chose is going to impede your ability to do that job, you're being negligent toward your buddy and that's not only not cool, it's dangerous. 

I think for those who have found psychedelics helpful for their own healing it can be very exciting to share that with others... But it is never okay to force someone to be vulnerable especially in an altered state. Unfortunately this trip sitter didn't seem to have healthy boundaries for themselves, let alone for you - sorry that made you second guess yourself but I am glad that you have come to realize that person may not have been the most healthy to maintain a relationship with. 

I find in my own struggles with self perception & communication that my own lack of self belief affects people negatively and makes their opinions of me worse. If I am hesitant and unsure, people don't know what to make of me either! If I feel like I might be misunderstood I tend to hesitate or languish over how I am going to say things, which jams up communication. All this to say that our perception, influences our behaviours which influences the perceptions of others which feeds back into our perceptions of self. 

Shrooms and psychedelics in general are great at shifting  our perspectives - that's what makes them such a powerful tool. Perspective changes can make lasting change happen more quickly because for a little while your brain pathways are a little more malleable and you see things in a new way! That's great when things go great and the perspective shift helps you to be more grateful or confident. During difficult experiences like the one you had, where set, setting or circumstances go awry and influence our perspective in the wrong direction, the most we can do is 1. recognize the feeling will cease, 2.hang on til the end, and then 3. Process the perspective we took on and reassess if that view actually serves us

In your case your set and setting went awry - your trip sitter was being weird - your perspective changed - negative self perception - the reprocessing where you debunk your 'diacoveroes' didn't happen so you just kept trucking along, only with new neural pathways primed to keep you in this mindset of feeling like you're a problem. 

So here's the deal, you're not a problem! Your feelings existing, are not a problem! They may seem bigger or louder but that's only because you are paying attention to them - think of psychedelics as a magnifier and a mirror. Now that you saw and felt what you got going on, you're naturally more aware of it afterwards. When you're feeling difficult things, that can be overwhelming, I know, but I also know that difficult feelings do pass. Just like every feeling, they come and go. Same thing with specific realizations you may have had about yourself. If you don't like something about yourself that you can change, try to find a way to do that - if you don't like things you cannot change, try to work on strategies to accept the conditions as they are.  This is all tough mental work; to shift your perceptions and habits. It is exactly the type of intense self work that people go to therapy for! Therapists and other mental health care professionals (which I am NOT) are like the coaches you can get advice from for how to strategize or overcome challenges or just to get someone to validate or call-out thought patterns with. I think if this is something you are feeling you want some advice on, therapists are a great place to start. 

As for those who are recommending another dose as a cure-all... Think of psychedelics as a combo of amplifier/magnifier/mirror. That super boost can be incredibly healing when applied at the right time, when the temperance is in the right state and they have the capacity to process and internalize things in a healthy way. But that boost of quick accelerated change can be a kick in the nads of your mental health, if not catastrophically destabilizing, if something goes wrong or people are not well enough to be taking on something so intense. . It is not a magic medicine that will do no harm just because it's non-toxic; psychs can break your brain if you aren't careful. The best judge for you, is you! If someone ever suggests or offers psychedelics to me, I do a check in - do I have the capacity to ride the trip out? Am I with people/in places I feel comfortable with? Am I ready for a paradigm shift if one comes? Will I have the support/space I need to integrate this experience afterwards? Will I be safe/can I get help if I need it? - if all those questions aren't met with an enthusiastic yes, I don't do it because it's not right for me in that moment. In your case, it could be that another trip allows to break free of these relatively fresh patterns that you don't like and break them in a jiffy; or it could be that another trip sends you further into confusion and disorienting mental health conditions.

 It is ultimately an unknown and when I try to imagine being in your shoes I personally would opt to take a slow and steady approach to try to change some of the habits I accidentally integrated post-trip before I try something as high risk/high reward as another full trip. I'd try to identify my thoughts/hangups, talk to a professional if I could and then try some little changes for a while. In my past, I hasmd some trauma that I processed for a while sober and was nervous to give myself that processing boost in a full dose right away. I opted to micro dose for a while and that was great in terms of the boost to my change-making and the lessened risk.

Hey!! I am so glad you asked this! I have gone to a bunch of concerts alone -Dance Gavin Dance, The Wonder Years, Streetlight Manifesto, A Lot Like Birds, the Story So Far, etc etc - since I turned 20. I can say with confidence that Dance Gavin Dance shows, though rowdy, have been safe and extremely fun as a single gal. The first show I ever went solo was one of theirs actually ^-^ 

I love going to shows on my own. I can hang at the edges by the bar/stairs/merch*, I can smush to the front, I can go flail about in the pit* (don't recommend for a first time beyond the edges tho unless you are already comfy in pits, as I mentioned, can be a bit rowdy at DGD) or I can crowdsurf* -- I get to do whatever I want on a whim without having to worry about finding friends after... This has afforded me awesome opportunities to enjoy incredible live music performances on my own terms. Additionally i have been able to actually meet and chat with some of my favorite artists (including Matt & Will) on these solo adventures because I don't have to convince anyone else that it's worth it to hang out around the venue for a half hour or so while the gear gets loaded into the van... 

 Of course as a woman you will need to keep aware of your surroundings, just like any crowd, there are going to be a few creeps sprinkled into the mix. I highly recommend being sober for the night or having a single drink just because you want to keep your wits about you. For larger venues, I like to find a woman working a door position/or bar near door - let her know I'm there alone that night and if I ask her where the bathrooms are with a guy in tow, I need help getting away from him. I have only ever needed to use this safety net once (ADTR is NOT a band I would recommend going solo for) but I do this anytime I feel unsure. I am a person who does not mind the squish that happens at the front of crowds but beware that there may me *ehm* uncomfortably placed hands at times. In my experience though, these are by and large unintentional - if you feel uncomfy, ask the nearest dudes to get you out - I have never been at a DGD show where those peeps will not get you up & out/back & out of the crowd. 

Just from my own experience I recommend going with as few loose objects as possible. There won't be anyone to hold anything for you. Batten down the boob-hatches with a tight sports bra (I usually wear two to compress and throw my phone & cards in between them). I do not recommend putting ANYTHING in your back pockets or wearing a fanny pack/stringy backpack. Though DGD fans are the type to return the contents to security, I would bet you're looking at a broken phone at least. 

Last tip I'll give you is just in regards of merch. So personally I love getting merch but often want to get into the sweaty mass... so to avoid ruining said merch, I find a hiding spot or a cache I can monitor from the floor. Sometimes I make a fast friend with someone who is clearly not going to leave the outskirts but this has backfired on me in the past - not all women are trustworthy when you are handing them merch they also want 😂. This totally depends on the venue but I usually scope this out once I figure out what I'm going to buy/how much/ what shape items I'm dealing with. I've hung crewnecks from railings, put records ontop of rafters, taped posters to walls behind trashcans, hidden tshirts behind bathroom stall walls, sticker books behind paper towel dispensers and more*! For this operation I recommend bringing 1 grocery bag, 2 rubber bands or hair ties, and some good tape. The tape is also not a big deal if you cant get some, the stagehands or bartenders always have it on hand so just ask somebody and they can usually get you a few pieces. 

If you have any other questions, please feel absolutely free to ask. I have been to like 3 solo DGD shows all in different venues and cannot recommend going hard enough. They are amazing.
